transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, um… I guess the main thing is my head just feels kind of foggy lately. Like I’m not as sharp as I normally am, and it’s been bothering me more than I expected. I work as a personal care aide, so I have to keep track of things and write client notes, and I’ve been catching myself making these little mistakes that I really don’t usually make.

It’s not huge things, but enough that I notice—like I’ll be writing something down and realize it’s not quite right, or I’ll go to do something and then just blank for a second, like, “Wait, what was I about to do?” And that’s not really like me. I’m usually pretty on top of those details, so it’s making me feel… I don’t know, frustrated and a little worried, I guess.
Do you use alcohol regularly, and if so, how often and how much do you typically consume?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that in a precise way. I don’t really keep track of it closely, so I’d hate to just throw out a number and have it be wrong. I guess I’d say it’s not something I’ve been thinking of as a major pattern, but if you’re asking for exact drinks per week or something like that, I’d probably need to sit and actually think it through.
Can you give me a more specific estimate of how many days a week you consume alcohol and approximately how many drinks you have on those days?

I honestly don’t have a clean number for you. I know that’s probably annoying because you’re asking pretty directly, but I don’t track it like that—like I don’t have a routine where it’s every Friday and Saturday or anything I can point to.

If I had to think about it, I’d need to go back over the last couple weeks and sort of count it out, because otherwise I’m worried I’d just be guessing. Some weeks it might be none, or maybe I’ll have something if I’m out or relaxing, but I’m not sitting here with a solid “three days a week, two drinks” kind of answer. I can try to pay attention going forward if that helps, but right now I’m not sure enough to give you a specific estimate.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you were drinking heavily, even if it wasn't on a regular weekly schedule?

I don’t know that I’d say “heavily,” but I guess it depends what you mean by that. Like, I can’t think of a period where I was drinking every day or where alcohol was the main thing going on in my life, if that’s what you’re asking.

There may have been times—like socially, or during certain stretches—where I had more than I usually would, but I’m having a hard time pinning down anything specific enough to say, “Yes, that was a heavy drinking period.” I don’t want to minimize it if there’s something I’m forgetting, but nothing is jumping out at me as a clear pattern like that.

Have you noticed any significant problems with your memory or confusion that has been getting worse over time, such as forgetting important information, getting lost in familiar places, or having trouble following conversations?

Yeah… I mean, that’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I don’t know if I’d describe it as getting lost or not understanding conversations exactly, but my head has felt kind of foggy, like I’m not as sharp as I usually am.

At work, I’ve been making these little mistakes in my client notes, and that bothers me because I’m usually pretty careful with that stuff. It’s not like huge mistakes, but enough that I notice and think, “Why did I write that wrong?” or “How did I miss that?” And sometimes I’ll be in the middle of doing something and suddenly forget what I was about to do, like I walked into a room or opened something up and then just blanked for a second.

It’s frustrating because it doesn’t feel like me. I’m not saying I’m completely confused all the time, but there’s definitely been this foggy, forgetful feeling that’s been worrying me.
Have you ever had any episodes where you couldn't remember chunks of time, like things you did or events you were part of, even if someone else told you about them later?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing, like whole chunks of time missing or someone saying, “You did this whole thing and you don’t remember it.” That hasn’t really happened to me that I can think of.

I mean, I’ve had those normal moments where I’ll forget why I walked into a room, or I’ll lose track of what I was about to say, which is frustrating, but that feels different from a blackout or losing hours. I don’t have people telling me about conversations or events that I have no memory of. If that had happened, I think it would really scare me, honestly.

So, no, I haven’t noticed anything like missing chunks of time. It’s more like brief fogginess or forgetful moments, not blank periods.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things that usually make you happy?

Yeah… I have. It’s kind of hard to explain because I’m still functioning, you know? Like I can get up, go to my shift, talk to people, do what I’m supposed to do, and I don’t think most people would look at me and immediately know something is wrong.

But lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s like before the day even starts, there’s already this weight there. And I can get through the motions, but inside I feel sad and kind of flat, like things aren’t really reaching me the way they normally would.

I don’t know if it’s “sad” in the crying-all-the-time sense, exactly. It’s more like this dull, heavy emptiness. Things that usually make me feel better don’t really land the same way. I’ll try to go about my day and act normal, especially around people I’m helping or talking to, but inside I just feel… low. Flat. Like I’m there, but not really myself.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy levels or felt unusually fatigued lately, even when you haven’t been physically active?

Yeah, definitely. That’s been really noticeable. Even on days where I haven’t done much, like I’m not running around or doing anything especially physical, my body still feels worn out. It’s not just being a little tired at the end of the day—it feels like I’m starting the day with less in the tank than I should have.

And with my work, simple things that I normally just do without thinking—like helping a client shower, getting things set up, moving around the house, or even carrying groceries in—those things take more out of me than they used to. I’ll finish something pretty routine and feel like, “Why am I this tired from that?” It’s frustrating because I know what my normal energy level is, and this doesn’t feel like it.

It’s not like I’m doing heavy labor all day every day, so the amount of fatigue feels out of proportion. I keep trying to push through it, but even basic stuff feels like it takes extra effort lately.
Have you lost interest or felt less pleasure in activities or hobbies that you usually enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I mean… I don’t know if I’d say I’ve completely lost interest in things. It’s more like I haven’t been reaching for them as much, but I can’t tell if that’s because I’m not enjoying them or because I’m just kind of going through the day and not thinking about it.

Like, there are things I usually like, and I guess if someone put them in front of me, I might still enjoy them some. But I haven’t really been paying close attention to whether they feel the same or not. I’m not sitting there thinking, “I hate this now,” or anything like that. It’s just… I don’t know. Maybe things feel a little muted, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it and say I’ve lost pleasure in everything.

So I guess my honest answer is: I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed a clear, dramatic loss of interest, but I also don’t feel as connected to things as I normally do.
Have you found that activities or things you usually enjoy don’t feel as rewarding or pleasurable to you lately?

I don’t know if I can say that clearly, honestly. I’ve been trying to think about that since you asked it the other way, and I’m not sure I have a clean answer.

It’s not like I pick something up that I usually enjoy and feel absolutely nothing, or like I suddenly hate it. It’s more… I guess I haven’t been noticing the reward from things as much, maybe? But I don’t know if that’s because the things themselves aren’t pleasurable or because I’m just kind of distracted and moving through the day on autopilot.

Like if something good happens or I do something I normally like, I might still be able to recognize, “Okay, this is nice,” but it doesn’t necessarily stick with me very long. It’s not a big, obvious drop where I can point to one hobby or activity and say, “That stopped feeling good.” It’s more vague than that.

So I’d say maybe things feel a little dulled down, but I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really been tracking it closely enough to say yes in a definite way.
Have you found that you no longer look forward to things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

I’m honestly not sure I’d put it as “no longer look forward to things.” That sounds a little stronger than what I can say for sure.

I think maybe I don’t anticipate things as much lately, or I don’t get as much of that little feeling of, “Oh, that’ll be nice,” ahead of time. But I also haven’t been paying close enough attention to know if that’s really happening or if I’m just tired and kind of getting through the day. Like, if there’s something I usually enjoy, I don’t necessarily dread it or think, “I don’t want to do that anymore.” It’s more like it doesn’t come to mind as easily, maybe.

If I still do the thing, I can sometimes enjoy it in the moment, at least somewhat. I just don’t know if I’m looking forward to it the way I normally would. It’s kind of blurry. So I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly stopped looking forward to everything, but maybe there’s a little less excitement there than usual.
Have you found it hard to feel any real pleasure or joy in things you used to enjoy, even when you're doing them?

I don’t know that I’d say it’s hard to feel any real pleasure, like across the board. That sounds more definite than what I can really say.

It’s more like… when I’m doing something I used to enjoy, I can sometimes still tell there’s something pleasant about it. Like I’m not completely numb to it. But maybe it doesn’t always land the same way, or I don’t stay with the good feeling very long. I’ll notice it for a second and then it kind of fades into the background, if that makes sense.

I also feel like I’m second-guessing myself a little because once you ask it that way, I start trying to measure it while I’m talking, and I’m not sure I’ve been paying enough attention in the moment. I haven’t had a clear experience of, “Wow, I used to love this and now I feel nothing.” It’s more vague than that.

So I guess my best answer is: maybe things feel a little less bright or less satisfying sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I clearly can’t feel joy or pleasure when I’m doing them.
Would you say that most of the time, you’re not getting any real pleasure out of things you used to enjoy, even when you’re doing them?

I don’t think I can say “most of the time” or “not getting any real pleasure,” no. That feels too absolute for what I’ve actually noticed.

I mean, I’m trying to answer it carefully because I don’t want to either exaggerate it or brush it off. When I do things I normally like, there are still moments where I can tell, okay, this is pleasant, or this is comforting, or I’m glad I did this. It’s not like everything has gone completely flat. But maybe the pleasure is quieter than usual, or I don’t hold onto it very long. Like it doesn’t carry me through the day the way it maybe would if I were feeling more like myself.

So if you’re asking whether I’m mostly unable to enjoy things, I’d say I’m not sure that’s true. I haven’t really tracked it closely enough to say that. It’s more that I’ve noticed some dullness or distance sometimes, but not a clear, constant absence of pleasure.
Have you found that, for most of the day, nearly every day, you don’t feel any pleasure or interest in almost all activities you used to enjoy?

I don’t think I can honestly say that, no. “For most of the day, nearly every day,” and “almost all activities” feels like a pretty big statement, and I don’t think I’ve noticed it that clearly.

I do have times where things feel kind of muted, like I said, or I’m not as interested as I’d normally expect to be. But it’s not like I wake up and go through the whole day feeling no pleasure in anything. There are still things that catch my attention or feel good while I’m doing them, even if it’s not always as strong or as lasting as I’d like.

I guess if I’m trying to be really precise, I’d say I’ve noticed some dullness here and there, maybe a little less excitement or less satisfaction at times. But I wouldn’t say it’s most of the day, nearly every day, and I wouldn’t say it’s almost everything I used to enjoy. That would be overstating it.
Have you noticed that you’ve stopped taking part in any activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy because they don’t seem worth it or you don’t care about them as much anymore?

I don’t think so, at least not in a clear way. I mean, I haven’t sat down and made a list of hobbies and checked off what I’m not doing anymore, so I’m trying not to overstate it. But I can’t really point to something and say, “I stopped doing that because I don’t care about it now,” or “it doesn’t seem worth it anymore.”

There are probably times I put things off or don’t get around to them, but that feels different to me than losing interest completely. If I do something I usually like, I can still get something out of it. Maybe not always as much as I’d hope, or not with the same excitement every time, but it’s not like I’ve abandoned everything I used to enjoy.

So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve really stopped taking part in activities or hobbies for that reason. I haven’t noticed that as a pattern.
Have you felt that, most days and most of the time, you don’t really care about things the way you used to, even things you used to enjoy a lot?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way, no. I don’t think I’ve had this broad feeling of just not caring about things most days, most of the time. That sounds more total than what I’ve been experiencing.

There are moments where I feel a little disconnected from things, or I don’t get as excited as I think I normally would. Like I might do something I usually enjoy and think, okay, this is fine, but it doesn’t hit quite the same. But I wouldn’t say I don’t care about it anymore. It’s more subtle than that, and it kind of comes and goes.

I’m trying to be accurate because if I say “yes,” it makes it sound like I’m indifferent to everything, and that doesn’t feel true. I still care about people, routines, things I like doing. Maybe sometimes it takes a little more effort to get into them, or the enjoyment doesn’t last as long, but I haven’t noticed a steady pattern of not caring most of the time.
Have you felt down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Yeah… I think that’s probably closer to what’s been going on. I don’t know if I’d say every single minute of the day, but lately I’ve been waking up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s like before anything even happens, before I’ve had coffee or gotten ready, it’s already there.

I can still get through my shift. I can talk to people, do what I need to do, answer questions, be polite, all of that. So from the outside I probably look more or less functional. But inside I feel sad and kind of flat, like I’m going through the motions and there’s this weight sitting there.

The “nearly every day” part… yeah, I’d say it’s been pretty consistent lately. I’m trying not to exaggerate, because some moments are better than others, but the overall feeling has been there most days, and for a lot of the day. It’s not just a bad hour here or there.
